headline: Payrolls beat and chips bounce lift the Nasdaq 1.1 percent as Kospi breaks below 5,000
subhead: October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected; AMD gained 11.0 percent, Intel 7.7, TSMC 6.3 and Tesla 4.2, while Samsung fell 6.4 percent in Seoul.

us.text: The S&P 500 rose 0.3 percent to 7,376.9 and the Nasdaq 1.1 percent as chipmakers recovered part of Thursday's rout; the Dow fell 0.5 percent.
October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected and unemployment fell to 4.1 percent, lifting bets on a December Fed hike.
Next week turns on October CPI on Tuesday, with FactSet's estimate at 3.9 percent year on year, and producer prices on Friday.

india.text: Nifty closed at 25,030.4 and Sensex at 81,028.0 on 6 November, led by M&M, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank; the price feed still shows 5 November.
Foreign investors bought a net 13,749.8 crore rupees of shares on 6 November and domestic institutions sold 5,968.7 crore, provisional data show.
The rupee gained 52 paise to settle at 93.89 per dollar on 6 November on a weaker dollar and strong equity inflows.

global.text: Kospi fell below 5,000 on 6 November after a plunge halted trading, as Samsung fell 6.4 percent and SK Hynix slid on AI regulation fears.
Europe fell on 6 November, with the STOXX 600 down about 1 percent and the DAX about 2 percent on the US tech rout and hot payrolls.
WTI fell 0.2 percent to 90.34 dollars, ending its biggest weekly drop since 2022, down 13.2 percent, on hopes of an Iran deal.

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 7.0 percent in the week to 5 November and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 13.2 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.6 percent and silver 5.8 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 2.1 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
